_note: Building templates for the static mesh pass. Each part sits on the building's ground (y = 0) at 'at' (x, y, z). Roof sizes are [width, rise, depth] of the walls they cover, with the ridge along x unless 'turn' rotates it. Textures name a palette entry below or an atlas tile; the palette uses placeholder tiles until art batch 1 lands.

tan_vats._note: Tanner's Row's sunk tan pits (harlow-bridge-areas.md 9): two rows of three square pits, plank rims just proud of the ground, the dark still liquor nearly to the brim, a plank walk between the rows and across. About 7.2 x 4.4.

bark_mill._note: Tanner's Row's bark mill (harlow-bridge-areas.md 9): four posts and a low mossy hip roof over a round stone bed filled with ground bark, an upright runner stone on edge in the track, its axle running from the king post out past the eaves both ways for the horse. About 5 x 5; the sweep reaches 3.7 out from the middle.

ice_blocks_0._note: Cut lake ice stacked on the Drowned Town's shore by the cutters' ramp (harlow-bridge-areas.md 11): blocks in a stepped pile, sawdust between the first courses. About 2.4 x 1.6.

ice_blocks_1._note: A smaller pile of cut lake ice (harlow-bridge-areas.md 11): four blocks, a sawdust layer, one on top, a broken piece beside. About 1.8 x 1.4.

sluice_gate._note: The Mill Pond's sluice gate (harlow-bridge-areas.md 10): a timber gate between two granite walls, the pond high behind it (-z) and the race low in front (+z), a gate frame over it and a flat hand wheel on the gate's stem. About 4 x 3.

ice_ramp._note: The ice cutters' ramp on the Drowned Town's east shore (harlow-bridge-areas.md 11): a plank slide with cleats on a solid timber bed, high on the shore (-z) and down to the ice (+z), side boards on posts. About 3 x 7.

recipes._note: Building kit recipes (decision 0008): everything except the footprint. A kit building in an area names one and may override storeys, pitch, mainRoof and variants. Opened buildings (decision 0021) also list rooms per storey: type (rooms.json), share of the floor, public (by the entrance), and which room types connect.

meetinghouse._note: Hardscrabble's meetinghouse (decision 0280): white, plain, gable end to the common, the door in the middle, two rows of tall windows, a short belfry with no spire, the stove's pipe for a chimney. One tall room inside.

shanty._note: The quarry cutters' shanty (decision 0281): grey boards, a mossy roof, small windows, a plank door and a stovepipe. Inside: the stove and the tally board.

shed._note: A tool shed in a yard (Obed Thayer's, decision 0310): grey boards, a mossy roof, a plank door, no chimney. Inside: shelves of tools.

rowhouse._note: Harlow Bridge's brick row house (decision 0382): 4 wide and 7 deep, two storeys and a garret with one dormer, the ridge along the street, the door to one side. Stand 4 to 6 side by side, touching, all turned the same way: party walls on both sides, so roofs and walls run on as one terrace and each unit carries the chimney on its right-hand party wall. End units are rowhouse_end.

rowhouse_end._note: The end of a brick terrace (decision 0382): a rowhouse whose open gable is a brick parapet with granite coping and its own chimney. Its neighbour is on its right; the unit at the other end of the row sets variants.party to ["left"].

shopblock._note: One shop of the Brick Block (decision 0382): 6 wide, 9 deep, two brick storeys, a shopfront (a shop window either side of the door) under a painted sign band with the shop's name (variants.signText). Stand four side by side as a terrace; the ends are plain brick gables.

inn._note: The Broken Tankard (decision 0382): the biggest building yet, about 14 by 8, two storeys of white clapboard with shutters, a slate roof, a porch the full length of the front, the door in the middle, a chimney on each end and the sign hanging from an iron bracket. Inside: the taproom and the kitchen; five rooms upstairs.

millhouse_office._note: The mill office under Harlow Bridge's clock tower (decision 0382): a two-storey brick office with a square brick tower rising through its left end, a clock on each face under a granite cornice, a white belfry and a low cap. The office downstairs; the clock's works room up.

meetinghouse_spire._note: Harlow Bridge's meetinghouse (decision 0382): the meetinghouse with a real steeple: a tower rising well above the ridge just inside the front, a louvered belfry and a tall octagonal spire. White clapboard, gable end to the street, the door in the middle. One tall room inside.

federal._note: Penhallow's house (decision 0382): a square brick Federal house, two storeys, a low hip roof, a pair of chimneys on each end wall, the door in the middle under its fanlight, granite trim.

mill_brick._note: A brick mill on the race (decision 0382): long, three storeys of weathered brick in even rows of windows, a low slate roof and a white belfry on the ridge. Give it a waterwheel landmark on the race side.

schoolhouse._note: The district schoolhouse (decision 0382): one room, one storey of red boards, gable end to the road with the door in the middle, a small white belfry over the door end, a stovepipe.

tailor._note: Euphemia Lord's tailor shop in Harlow Bridge (decision 0383): the store with a bow window and the tailor's room inside.

tannery._note: The Rowes' tannery on Tanner's Row (harlow-bridge-areas.md 9): a long low one-storey shed of weathered grey boards, a mossy shingle roof with a long roofed smoke vent on the ridge, a plank door and small windows. Place it about 14 x 6. Rooms from rooms.json plans: the beam house and a storeroom.

grogshop._note: The grog shop on Tanner's Row (harlow-bridge-areas.md 9): a small rough tavern, one storey and a garret under a steep roof with a dormer, weathered grey boards, a mossy roof, a sign over the plank door and a stovepipe. Place it about 7 x 5. Rooms from rooms.json plans: the taproom, and the garret above (an interior file for the garret needs source storeys 2, since the garret is in the roof).

fallbacks._note: Stand-ins for textures whose art isn't exported yet (decision 0382): used only while the atlas lacks the name, so the real tile takes over by itself.
